Convening map

Evidence you can open

Quick readMore contextTechnical detailSpeaker notes

These six repositories are the starting points identified in the supplied materials. Specific result claims should be checked against their dated reports. Repository access and current readiness may vary.

  • Computational-Spacetime-Dynamics-Research: the research campaign records
  • KosMojAMD: the Mojo on AMD modernization case study
  • gkos-standard: the evidence-governance pre-standard
  • GKOS-Engine: the TypeScript reference engine
  • GKOS-Engine-Rust: the Rust implementation effort
  • GKOS-Observatory: the demonstration

What useful evidence records should preserve:

  • Exact experiment and source identifiers.
  • Failed, blocked, superseded, and inconclusive outcomes.
  • Original timestamps, with execution date kept separate from publication date.
  • Hardware, software, and environment boundaries.
  • Links from summaries to the underlying reports, manifests, logs, and artifacts.
  • Corrections as visible successor records, never silent rewrites.
  • Explicit separation of backend agreement, scientific accuracy, performance, and production readiness.

Related work, identified in the supplied materials, with current status requiring review: LLM_Engine_Rust-Over-GGML (archived comparison), LLM_Engine_Mojo, LLM_Engine_MojoRust (gated rebuild), GKOS-Engine-Lite, gkos-hindsight-governance, model-capability-manifest-standard, Kosmos-Oden, Kosmos-Oden-Lite, Kosmos_Research_Studio_Lite, Marshal-008-OS, theMarshal-Core-Rust, Hypatia, temporal-modulation-alcubierre, Paper01.

The three Rust/Mojo engine repositories overlap historically. Their roles and evidence boundaries need to be reconciled so a visitor can tell immediately what was attempted, what was measured, what was learned, and which repository now carries the authoritative evidence.

Before any private repository goes public it gets a disclosure review: credentials, personal data, internal network details, large artifacts, licensing, and any claim that exceeds the retained evidence.

Participant proposals for the Widener-led, NSF-funded convening. Project examples include documented results, work in development, and proposed pilots.
